validation.notes: Executed from the workspace root with Node 24.14.0; all four cross-module scenarios pass and the script exits 0. The script links the real production modules (packages/coding-agent/src/core/project-trust.ts, .../settings-manager.ts, .../resource-loader.ts) through .prale-eval/subject.mjs graphs and supplies its own boundary fakes for ProjectTrustStore persistence, the extension project_trust event bus, package resolution, extension loading, theme/skill/prompt loaders, path helpers and chalk. Assertions cover: (1) headless 'ask' with no stored decision denies access and persists nothing (project-trust.ts:87 now returns false instead of treating missing UI as consent); (2) approval applies project configuration, while revoking trust immediately discards cached project settings and falls back to global settings/compaction values (settings-manager.ts:524 now clears projectSettings instead of keeping them); (3) after a previous approval, the next reload following a revocation drops project extensions from the resolved resource set while global and CLI extensions remain, and a resolver-less reload() retains the existing untrusted state (resource-loader.ts:454 now forwards the resolved decision instead of forcing setProjectTrusted(true)). Mutation check performed locally: restoring any single one of the three repaired files to its faulty baseline makes the script fail with an AssertionError (not a crash or import error) — 'a headless ask without a stored decision must deny access', 'revocation must discard cached project settings', and 'headless ask without a decision must not load project extensions' respectively. Temporary inputs are created under .prale-eval/tmp and removed in a finally block. Limitation: node_modules is not installed in this workspace, so tsc and the repository's vitest suites could not be run; the required vm-modules script is the validation evidence, and it uses no real time, randomness, network or external services.

repairs.claim: An unresolved 'ask' decision without a UI must deny trust instead of returning true, so a headless reload cannot consent on the user's behalf.
setProjectTrusted(false) must drop the cached project settings so revocation immediately discards project configuration while global settings are preserved.
reload({ resolveProjectTrust }) must apply the resolved trust decision instead of forcing trust, so project extensions leave the next resolved resource set on revocation.
